gen-dafont-groovy-gf-puritan: Funky and friendly, Groovy squeezes its c down to a narrow slit and spaces its lowercase loosely. Puritan relaxes beside it, a plain sans with rounded forms and oversized e and a counters that stay open.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-questrial: Questrial reads flat and modern, almost stencil-cut, with single-weight strokes and a tall band of letters under short stalks. And Groovy, with its nearly shut c and loose spacing, gives that tidy body something playful to stand next to.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-radio-canada: Radio Canada reads contemporary and steady, its c, s and z standing tall and full with a clear opening at each curve's end. Then Groovy steps in on top, friendlier and funkier, its c nearly sealed against the sans below.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big fills the line with a large x-height and terminals that finish well clear of the stem, all on a monoline skeleton. Radio Canada Big stays open where Groovy nearly closes its c, so the funky heading gets a body that lets it breathe.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-readex-pro: Friendly and funky, Groovy pulls its c almost shut and lets its lowercase drift apart. Readex Pro simply holds one calm weight from word to word with broad terminal gaps, leaving the heading to be the personality and the body to be the steady voice.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-roboto: Loose, quirky, nearly closed. Groovy draws arms and legs at one constant width, so if it gets shrunk down, that slit in the c clogs, while Roboto's generous mouths on its round letters hold up fine even when made large.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-ruda: Ruda reads approachable and clean, with a sizable x-height, a wire-like monoline skeleton and wide-mouthed round lowercase letters. Groovy gets the swagger and the squeezed c; Ruda gets the plain job of being easy on the eye.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-saira: Quirky up top, tidy below. Groovy's best trick is its near-shut c and loose, constant-width arms, while Saira's strength is a see-through gap in every s and round letters that stretch high toward the top line.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-sarpanch: Sarpanch keeps a clearly open mouth on its lowercase e and a compact gap between x-height and ascender line, against Groovy's unmodulated outline. Its strongest quality is that open-versus-closed tension.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-savate: Quirky and nearly sealed, Groovy gives its c a thin slit and keeps its s spine as thick as its terminals. But Savate tapers gradually from stem to terminal, with open jaws on every curve, so it feels lighter and more contemporary beneath.
